title: RREQ hop_limit not clamped on write_to, only on parse
description:
File: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs
Line: 365

Issue: Rreq.write_to() serializes hop_limit directly without clamping to MAX_HOP_LIMIT. While from_bytes() correctly clamps incoming hop_limit to 15 (line 348), write_to() will serialize any value set by the caller.

Trigger: Code that constructs an Rreq manually with hop_limit > 15 (e.g., hop_limit: 255) and calls write_to() will produce a message that, when parsed by a peer, gets clamped to 15 - creating asymmetry between sent and received values.

Impact: Data inconsistency between sender's in-memory state and receiver's parsed value. Could cause confusion in logging/debugging.

Suggested fix: Either clamp hop_limit in write_to(), or enforce the invariant at construction time by making hop_limit private and providing a constructor that clamps.
close_reason: Invalid: The finding claims from_bytes clamps hop_limit (line 348) but write_to does not. This is factually incorrect - from_bytes at line 310 does NOT clamp (just reads data[1] directly), and line 348 is in Rrep struct definition not parsing logic. Both methods are symmetric; neither clamps. No asymmetry exists.
